title: S2 semantic mutation support: in-memory source-edit runner with the plan s5 outcome classes
objective: Build the instrument S3/S4 will use to apply committed semantic source edits to frozen code in memory and classify each one, without overwriting any source file.
problem: Plan s5: distinguish proposed, applicable, duplicate, executed, killed, survived, equivalent, syntax/import error and timeout; errors are not semantic kills; run the unchanged suite first; a survivor needs a behavioural witness; absence of an observed difference is not equivalence (uncertain equivalence is unresolved). Edits are data files committed before execution; the runner reads them, compiles the edited module in memory, runs the frozen suite, and writes a per-edit row with flush.
non_goals: The runner never decides equivalence: it records UNRESOLVED and the reviewer adjudicates
No attack contents (the reviewer writes those)
Python >= 3.8 standard library only; no package installation (MWO-0004 R2)
evidence_required: RED/fire test: a known killing edit, a known surviving edit, a syntax-error edit and a timeout edit on a toy module, each expected class asserted, failing before implementation
GREEN: all four classified correctly; no file under rso/slice001 modified (checked by hash before/after)

acceptance.condition: the four control edits classify as expected; source tree hashes unchanged

authority: operator directive 2026-10-03 s9, s11 (roles/Achilles/prompts/2026-10-03_rso_builder_cell/01_OPERATOR_DIRECTIVE_verbatim.md); decomposed by Palamedes under C-004-T000

resource_ceiling.note: Counts toward the slice caps fixed by C-004-OP1 (NEXT_ROUND_PLAN_v0.4 s6 proposal: 30 CPU-minutes total, 0 GPU, 0 cloud, 100 MB new artifacts, 12 top-level validation launches; mutation children count toward CPU). Stop at the first exhausted cap and keep partial results.
